special_features.feature: Square 52 m plan divided diagonally into four triangular shafts that stop at different heights; only one triangular prism reaches the top
Diagonal bracing on every face, expressed by aluminium covers flush with the facade; diagonals cross each facade from about the sixth level to the top
Megastructural steelwork expressed outside by naturally anodised panels that are part of the curtain wall
Horizontal members of the X were hidden so the faces read as a chain of diamonds rather than X + horizontal bars (feng-shui change)
Number of X shapes on the outward face of each shaft: 1, 2, 3 and 5 (massing diagram)
Shaft heights follow 1, 2, 3, 5 units (Fibonacci)

Sloped (inclined) glass roofs at the top of each shaft; SkyscraperPage heights: bottom of lowest slope 262 ft (79.9 m), bottom of another slope 433 ft (132 m), top of second-highest slope 691 ft (210.6 m), bottom of top slope 946 ft (288 m)
Two masts on top (decorative)
Granite podium (said to represent the Great Wall)
15-storey atrium; glazed with 25 mm thick pattern-cut glass

x_bracing_modules.faces: All four outer faces. Each outer face belongs to one triangular shaft. Inner (diagonal) faces of the taller shafts also show bracing where they rise above shorter shafts.
x_bracing_modules.how_derived: X counts from the Wikimedia Commons massing diagram. Module height derived by me from SkyscraperPage slope heights (79.9, 132, ~184, 288 m bottoms are ~52 m apart) and matches the 52 m plan width (PCF) and the class notes saying horizontal bracing frames sit at every 13th floor and a 12-storey major bracing configuration. Not an official figure.

buildings.crown_top: Single triangular prism with a steeply sloped glass roof, topped by two thin masts (to 367.4 m).
buildings.night_lighting: Part of the Symphony of Lights / Victoria Harbour Lighting Plan; lighting consultants listed include Fisher Marantz Stone, Laservision and Martin Professional. Typical look (not described in sources): white outline lights along the diagonal bracing and edges.
